note: `debrief` runs when messages arrived while the session was working. Its load-bearing output is `unanswered`, and the distinction that governs it is whether the session *took the message on*: `adjust` and `respond_now` mean it changed course because of the arrival and now owns it, while `continue` and `abort` leave the message queued for a session of its own. Reporting the latter as unanswered raises an alarm about a message already in hand — seen live, where the note was stale before anything read it.

cases.note: The clear case. A second person asks something unrelated to the running task, the session carries on and answers the original question, and nobody ever answers theirs. The session re-scheduled around this message — it owns it — and then never addressed it.

message.text: harness, what is the difference between a mutex and a semaphore?

arrivals.author: olav
arrivals.text: which one would you use for a connection pool?

completed.name: respond
completed.content: A mutex has ownership — only the locking thread unlocks it — and protects a critical section. A semaphore has no ownership and counts access to a pool of resources.
